## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4, titled *Purāṇacīvara* ("Having a nun wash a used robe"), is a monastic disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who causes an unrelated nun to wash or dye a used robe incurs an offense requiring both the relinquishment of the robe and confession [SuttaCentral]. English translation of the text has been made available by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

This training rule is broadly represented across early Buddhist traditions. SuttaCentral records parallels in the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Np 4) and Parivāra (Np 4), as well as corresponding Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa rules (frequently designated as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4 or 5) across Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Gāndhārī, alongside Mūlasarvāstivāda Bhikkhunī Vinaya rules [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates high formulaic overlap across 118 other Pali texts, particularly Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 17 (sharing segment range §1.30–2.2.27), Np 6, Np 9, Np 5, Np 8, Np 25, and Pācittiyas 25 and 26 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also establishes cross-language alignments with Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* recensions, Chinese Āgama material, and Tibetan Vinaya treatises and commentaries including the *Vinayasaṃgraha* and Prātimokṣa commentaries [DharmaNexus].
